analysis:
The supplied changes are documentation only: docs/provider/cli-reference.md (three head-text excerpts) and docs/reference/configuration.md (a patch adding a 'Runtime metallib snapshots' section, plus an empty-patch metadata unit 8d39ffcfaa638a3c:0). No executable code changed, so no new attack surface and no regression of TB-002/TB-009/TB-011 assumptions.

The docs describe existing behavior, and nothing in them contradicts the threat model: enrollment guidance is explicitly not an App Attest grant; the OS choice never grants serving authorization; MDM removal needs fresh coordinator readiness; `unenroll` elevates only the fixed read-only profile inventory command; restart waits for fresh authorization; and `report` bounds log collection and drops key identifiers.

The new configuration.md section documents TMPDIR as the runtime metallib snapshot directory (BinaryHasher.makeRuntimeMetallibSnapshot). It says invalid values fail snapshot creation without fallback and that the setting changes no binding checks. This is consistent with T-013/T-034 integrity assumptions, but the underlying source was not supplied, so I could not verify those claims. Residual risk for a later pass: a user-controlled TMPDIR could point to an attacker-writable directory if the snapshot's anonymity or binding is weaker than documented. This cannot be assessed from docs alone, and the code in BinaryHasher.swift was not in the batch.

Cross-file interactions to check, if code changes are in other batches: the doc claims about /v1/enroll proofs, legacy MDM cohort gating, and App Attest removal readiness are described in TB-009 and TB-011 but implemented elsewhere. No finding is raised from docs alone.
